added_failures_note: measured: the reviewed manifest's baseline_suite and after_suite both record one failing id, tests/test_crew_obligations.py::test_obligations_reads_scoring_without_observing_or_dispatching, so the head adds no failure against the base.

assertion_analysis.condition_to_fail: The per-file identity read is reached on a cache hit, or the directory identity does not invalidate the cache, so a second call stats run files or returns stale namings.
The re-read count stays zero after a record is rewritten through the store's atomic rename, or the sweep does not find the rewritten document.
The previous tick's namings are reused without re-reading, so the removed run's naming survives.
Only if record_station_read_counts fails to store, or station_read_counts fails to parse what it stored; the values are the ones the test itself supplied, so no read producing no count fails it.

findings.text: record_station_read_counts and station_read_counts (line 365) have no caller anywhere in reckon/ or tests/ except the test, and namings_reread_count at reckon/crew/obligations.py:1307 has none at all, so neither read's re-read count ever reaches the station tick record the done_when's fifth case requires.

the landed evidence fragment states reckon/crew/obligation_snapshot.py carries both reads' counts into the station's tick record, which no production caller does, so the record a reader lands on the section asserts a behaviour the head does not have.

the fifth case passes namings=1 and attempts=2 into record_station_read_counts and asserts those same values come back from station_read_counts, a round trip that holds whether or not any read produces a count, so it survives the regression it was added to catch; the negative control only strips the helper itself.

LIVE builds 30 live pointers but is never used, so the fixture holds 2,000 run files and zero live pointers, and the done_when's live-pointer population and the case where a pointer move re-reads exactly one run are not exercised.

the cache is keyed on the runs directory's identity alone while _run_namings reads ledger.runs, which merges crew.json with the per-run documents (reckon/ledger.py:load), so a row that changes only in the aggregate leaves the namings stale until some run document moves.

the gate log the manifest names as test_logs records its revision as "504545c1bc + working tree", not the landed head bca9b53dbf, so the receipt alone cannot show the landed tree passed; re-running the test at head gives 3 passed, EXIT=0.
